a.text: Sukandar represented Indonesia at the Womens Asian Team Chess Championship in 2009.

b.text: Sukandar represented Indonesia at the 2009 Asian Indoor Games.

a.text: Sukandar represented Indonesia at the 2013 Asian Indoor and Martial Arts Games.

b.text: In December 2013, Sukandar won two individual gold medals for rapid and blitz chess at the 2013 Southeast Asian Games.

a.text: Sukandar qualified to play in the Womens World Championship 2014, which was postponed to 2015.

b.text: In 2014, Sukandar won for the second time the Asian Womens Championship in Sharjah, United Arab Emirates.

a.text: Sukandar's 2014 victory qualified her for the knockout Womens World Championship 2016.

b.text: In 2016, Sukandar shared first place in the Master section of the Continental Class Championships in Herndon, Virginia.

a.text: Sukandar won the G section of the 2015 Moscow Open with a score of 7.5/9.

b.text: At the Womens World Chess Championship 2015, Sukandar was knocked out in the first round by Salome Melia.

a.text: In 2018, Sukandar was the best female player at the Doeberl Cup by scoring 5.5/9 points.

b.text: In November 2018, Sukandar won the 2018 Hjorth Open by scoring 7.5/9 points.
